M1.reason: Measured silhouette overlap is 0.621 front/back, 0.385 left/right and 0.347 top/below. All three are far below the 0.80 needed. The pose also differs: the original is mid-stride with its arms down at its sides, while the reproduction stands straight-legged with one forearm thrust forward horizontally (front, left and right views). In the top and below views the arms and legs are spread differently.

M2.reason: Measured size is 33.3 x 21.7 x 68 for the original and 22.9 x 28.1 x 73.1 for the reproduction. Length is 31% off and width is 30% off, both well beyond 10%. Height is 7.5% off, which is within 10%.

M3.reason: The main parts are there: bald head, glasses, red/black striped tie, white lab coat, shirt, belt, white trousers, brown shoes and hands. Some parts are missing or wrongly shaped. The original's grey fringe of hair at the sides and back of the head is missing (back and side views), and the coat has no lapels or open front shaped like the original's. The hands are rounded blobs. The shoulders are boxy slabs that stick out above the arms (front and back-right views), and the forward forearm is a separate tube held out in front.

M4.reason: Measured mean colour difference (deltaE) is 17.4, above the line of 15. The 'below' view is worst at 26.7. The shirt is a pale sky blue where the original's is dark navy-slate (front and front-left/right views). In the run frames the arms and trousers read mid-grey against the original's off-white. The coat, skin and shoes are broadly right.

M5.reason: The tie stripes, glasses and some cloth grain on the coat are there. The original's detail is missing: the face has no features, there is no hair, and the shirt pocket and collar detail and the creases on the coat and trousers are gone. The reproduction's surfaces are flat and smooth by comparison.

M6.reason: At game size it reads as a lab-coated scientist, but not as this one. It is bald with no hair fringe and has a featureless face. The bright light-blue shirt is wrong, the body is stiff and boxy with slab shoulders, and the pose is wrong. A player would see a different, cruder model.

M7.reason: The front faces the original's front, the model is upright, and the feet stand on the ground plane at the origin as the original's do in all six side views.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. It has 1096 triangles against 740 for the original, under the 1480 allowed. Nothing open, inside out or floating is visible in the ten views.

C1.reason: The run cycles its legs and stays roughly in one piece, but it does not move like the original. The forward forearm stays rigidly horizontal at chest height in nearly every frame (RUN2 1, 3, 6, 19, 22), and in frames 1 and 22 it reads as detached from the grey upper arm. The torso and coat stay stiff and upright, with none of the original's forward lean or arm swing. The feet also sit well below the row's reference line in every reproduction frame, while the original's feet rest on its line, which suggests the body sinks.
